lens.message:
Here's the shift, from Tess's pushback: SMS stops being the default demo channel. In evaluator and skeptic contexts it's spam-coded — 'requiring someone to text might actually be a real downside' — so first-touch conversations move to a chat widget on the share page, and SMS stays scoped to high-trust, post-consent contexts. It changes how we approach the Demo 1 channel decision (explicit, not drift), the SMS onramp investment (stop if verification fails again), and share architecture (one widget per share ID, nothing auto-assigned to you).

The before/after, on 'Narrowing the SMS Framing, Not Killing It' in today's write-up:

As written: 'SMS remains viable for high-trust, post-consent, consumer-viral contexts — the channel works where the sender is already welcome. A chat widget on the share page is the right fit for evaluator, skeptic, first-touch, and demo contexts — no number, no verification, no opt-in form, no spam frame. … This is a scoping, not a replacement.'

Through the shift: this is the operating rule, not a caveat. Channel choice follows trust context — the share page carries the trust, so the widget inherits it; SMS keeps only the contexts where the sender is already welcome; per-user toll-free verification stops being load-bearing for demo strategy; and Demo 1's live SMS (Apr 13 Keystone) becomes an explicit decision, with a second verification failure as the signal to stop investing in the SMS onramp.

Right read?

What it moves: no other documents are in view for this stream, so I can't list what shifts yet — but this should touch everything that states the SMS demo framing, the per-user verification cost, and the Demo 1 plan. Want me to pull the documents and apply this across everything it moves?
